name: reasoning-controller
description: Adaptive Reasoning Controller: picks the right effort level (low to max) for every task and actually sends it with each model request via turn.step.

mode.title: Reasoning: working mode
mode.description: auto = level per task; balanced = balanced (no MAX); quality = quality first; speed = speed first; manual = fixed level (see manualLevel).

maxLevel.title: Reasoning: max level
maxLevel.description: The highest level the controller may choose on its own.

minLevel.title: Reasoning: min level
minLevel.description: The lowest level the controller may choose on its own.

priority.title: Reasoning: cost/time priority
priority.description: efficiency = maximum efficiency; balanced = balanced; quality = maximum quality. Applies in auto mode.

manualLevel.title: Reasoning: level in manual mode
manualLevel.description: session = leave the session level set with /effort unchanged.

autoEscalation.title: Reasoning: automatic escalation
autoEscalation.description: Raises the level for further model requests when a task turns out harder than expected (repeated tool failures, or Claude asks for it).

showDecision.title: Reasoning: show decision
showDecision.description: Shows the detected task, the level and a short reason in the transcript before each task.

aiClassification.title: Reasoning: AI classification
aiClassification.description: Lets Claude Code's small, fast model choose the level. off = local analysis only; unclear = only when the local analysis is unsure; always = before every new task (one short request and a little latency per task). Limits and modes still apply.

showStatusLine.title: Reasoning: show the status line
showStatusLine.description: The status line (Mode ◆ AUTO  ·  Reasoning ▰▰▰▱▱ HIGH  ·  Limit MAX): under the prompt in the terminal (click the mode for the settings, the meter for the next task's level), above the input in the desktop app.

rules.title: Reasoning: rules
rules.description: Your own rules, separated by ';'. text=level (exactly), text>=level (at least), text<=level (at most); text is matched in the prompt. Example: /quick=low; infra/>=high; readme<=medium

learnFromOverrides.title: Reasoning: learn from my overrides
learnFromOverrides.description: When you often pick another level with /reasoning for the same kind of task, adjust that kind by one level (after 3 overrides). Keeps task types and level steps only, never prompt text.

projectProfiles.title: Reasoning: project profiles
projectProfiles.description: Limits per project folder, separated by ';'. folder-part: min=level max=level. Example: playground: max=high; payments-api: min=medium
